citations.title: Human tendon adaptation in response to mechanical loading: a systematic review and meta-analysis of exercise intervention studies on healthy adults.
citations.notes: 27 studies, 37 interventions (Achilles/patellar, 264 participants), all >=8 weeks. Tendon stiffness SMD 0.70 (CI 0.51-0.88). Stiffness adaptation significantly depends on loading INTENSITY (p<0.05, I2=0%), not contraction type; SMD trend higher (not significant) for >=12-week interventions. Stiffness changes attributed to material more than morphological properties. Gives DURATION (>=8w, trend >=12w) and the intensity-dependence; does NOT give a tendon-vs-muscle adaptation-speed ratio.

citations.title: Dumbbell versus cable lateral raises for lateral deltoid hypertrophy: an experimental study.
citations.notes: 24 resistance-trained men and women, 8 weeks, 2 sessions/week, 5 sets of lateral raises to momentary failure. Within-participant design: each arm randomly allocated to cable or dumbbell. CRITICALLY, shoulder ab/adduction ROM was STANDARDISED AND MATCHED between conditions. Lateral deltoid thickness rose 3.3-4.6%; Bayesian analysis gave moderate support for the null univariately (BF=0.27 distal, 0.22 proximal) and extreme support multivariately (BF<0.01). Tests whether the IMPLEMENT matters with ROM held constant - it does not. Does NOT test whether loading the lengthened position matters, because equalizing ROM removes exactly that variable.
